=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 1778-1800 (within the deferral branch)
  Problem: The deferral branch does not reset `LAST_ACTIVITY`, so the diagnostic `IDLE` timer keeps growing across deferred polls and can overstate how long the step has been idle.
  Why: When the per-step stall deferral triggers (idle ≥ REVIEW_TIMEOUT but step_elapsed < STEP_INACTIVITY_LIMIT), the loop continues with `continue` without updating `LAST_ACTIVITY`. This causes the logged `IDLE` value to be based on the original activity timestamp from before the long step started, potentially reporting values like "idle 2500s" even though the step itself has only been running for say 1800s. This is misleading in logs but does not affect the actual stall gate logic which uses `STEP_ELAPSED`.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 1720-1726 (the fallback reuse block)
  Problem: A step-boundary race can clear the per-step stall deferral when `CURRENT_STEP` changes before `started_at` is reported, letting a healthy in-progress step fall through to the normal stall path.
  Why: The fallback only reuses timing when `CURRENT_STEP` matches `LAST_STEP_GUARD_NAME` or is empty. If the Jobs API returns a new step name but no `started_at` (transient step boundary), the condition `{ [ -z "${CURRENT_STEP:-}" ] || [ "${CURRENT_STEP}" = "${LAST_STEP_GUARD_NAME:-}" ] }` will fail if the step name changed, causing the timing reuse to be skipped. This leaves `CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT` empty, and the deferral guard at lines 1778-1802 will be bypassed, potentially misclassifying a healthy long-running step as stalled.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: wait-review loop, lines ~1720-1728 (last-run-diff hunk)
  Problem: A step-boundary race can clear the per-step stall deferral when `CURRENT_STEP` changes but `started_at` is briefly absent from the Jobs API response for that poll.
  Why: The fallback reuses last-seen timing only when `CURRENT_STEP` matches `LAST_STEP_GUARD_NAME` or is blank. If a new step has started and its `started_at` has not yet been reported, `CURRENT_STEP` will be the new step name (non-blank, non-matching), so the fallback does not fire and the guard loses its `STEP_ELAPSED` signal for that entire poll cycle.
  SEVERITY: NIT (defers to the next poll tick; the guard recovers once the API reports `started_at` for the new step, but that single poll can still be a false stall if the inactivity timer has been close to the limit for a long healthy run)
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: wait-review loop deferral branch, lines ~1794-1801 (last-run-diff hunk)
  Problem: The deferral `continue` branch does not reset `LAST_ACTIVITY`, so the diagnostic `IDLE` timer keeps growing across deferred polls and will report a much larger idle time than the step has actually been idle.
  Why: This is not a functional failure — the stall gate uses `STEP_ELAPSED`, not `IDLE` — but the diagnostic output will be misleading. Once `STEP_ELAPSED` eventually reaches `STEP_INACTIVITY_LIMIT`, the fallthrough to the normal stall path will report an `IDLE` value that is inflated by every preceding deferred poll, potentially confusing operators reading the failure log.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
